items.title: Eddie Locke interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, NY, January 13, 2001
items.q: I mean Mingus did that, but he didn’t play ugly.

ctx.x: You know you’ve seen jazz go through lots of things. Was there a time in your career where you felt jazz was going in the wrong direction?

Oh a lot of times I thought it was going wrong. And it’s for the same reason that I think that — it’s not the kind of music you play, it’s the way you play it that I don’t like. Like people play, I’ve heard guys play like the avante garde stuff. It wasn’t so much that I disliked what they were playing as it was the way they were playing it. You know, the harshness they had with the music. They played ugly. You don’t have to play ugly. You could be creative and do all that stuff without being ugly too. You know if…
That’s a good observation. It’s like almost the musicians, if they’re going to get rid of the harmonic limitations and the time, does that mean you have to play ugly?
